IS: 2891 -1975 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

WOODEN HANDLES FOR 

FELLING AXES AND HAND AXES 



( First Revision ) 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 23 October 1975, after the draft finaUzed by the 
Timber Stores Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil 
Engineering Division Council. 

0.2 The general requirements for wooden tool handles are covered by 
IS : 620-1975*. A series of standards have been prepared for various hand 
tools and for use with these hand tools a series of standards for the 
corresponding wooden handles are being prepared. This standard deals 
with the wooden handles for felling axes and hand axes conforming to 
IS : 703-1966t. 

0.3 This standard was first published in 1964. In this revision besides 
permitting some tolerances on the length of handles, test requirements have 
also been included. 

0.4 In the formulation of this standard, due weightage has been given to 
the International co-ordination among the standards and practices 
prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices 
in the field in this country. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing 
the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960:j:. 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should 
be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



♦General requirements for wooden tool handles ( third revision ). 

fSpecification for axes ( revised ). 

:|:Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ) 



IS : 2891 - 1§75 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requirements of wooden handles for the 
following four types of axes conforming to IS : 703-1966*. 

a) Axe, hand; c) Axe, felling, estate pattern; and 

b) Axe, felling; d) Axe, felling, trade pattern. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 620-19751 
shall apply. 

3. SPECIES OF TIMBER 

3.1 Handles for Hand Axes — These shall be manufactured from any of 
the timber species specified for Class III handles in IS : 620-1975t. 

3.2 Handles for Felling Axes — These shall be manufactured from any 
of the timber species specified for Glass I handles in IS : 620-1975f. 

3.3 Handles for Felling Axes, Estate and Trade Pattern — These shall 
be manufactured from any of the timber species specified for Class I 
handles in IS : 620-1 975t. 

4. RECIUIREMENTS OF BLANKS 

4.1 The blanks shall be well-seasoned to a moisture content not exceeding 
15 percent and not less than 8 percent. The blanks shall be free from 
centre heart (pith), any kind of decay (rot), checks, shakes, splits 
( except hair splits ), borer holes, warp and any other defect except those 
permitted in the finished handles in IS : 620-19751. 

4.2 The green blanks, if so desired, may also be given treatment as given 
in Appendix A to prevent cracking and splitting. 

5. MANUFACTURE 

5.1 The handles shall be manufactured from selected blanks prepared as 
above and shaped as shown in Fig. 1 to 3. 

5.2 It is recommended that immediately after manufacture, all the handles 
be dipped in raw linseed oil at room temperature as this treatment retards 
changes in the moisture content. 

6. DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES 

6.1 Dimensions — The handles shall conform to the dimensions as shown 
in Fig. 1 to 3.

6.2 Tolerances — The following tolerances shall be permissible on the 
diameter of the handles: 



+ 3 mm 
— mm 

± 2 mm 



a) Where the head of the tools fits 

b) At other places 

7. OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

7.1 Workmanship and finish, permissible defects, treatment, and sampling 
shall be as specified in IS : 620-1975*. 

8. TESTS 

8.1 In addition to the tests specified in IS : 620-1975*, the following tests 
shall also be carried out on the finished handles selected in accordance 
with the sampling procedure given in IS : 620-1975*. 

8.2 Drop Test — The handle shall be held horizontally and dropped from 
a height of 1'25 m on a concrete surface, 10 times continuously. 

8.3 Impact Test — The handle shall be fitted with a dummy head of 
approximately the same weight as that of the tool. It shall then be struck 
with a reasonable force, on a hardwood surface, 10 times continuously. 

♦General requirements for wooden tool handles ( third revision ). 

5 



8.4 At the end of the tests specified in 8.2 and 8.3, there shall be no visible 
damage, chips or cracks at any portion of the handle. 

9. SAMPLING 

9.1 The method of drawing representative samples of handles and criteria 
for conformity shall be as prescribed in IS : 620-1975*. 

10. MARKING 

10.1 Unless otherwise specified, each handle shall be legibly and indelibly 
marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark, 
if any, name of timber species and the year of manufacture. In addition, 
the type of the axe for which the handle is required, shall be marked as 
shown bclovv: 

Type Marking Code 

a) Axe, hand AH 

b) Axe, felHng AF 

c) Axe, felling, estate pattern AFEP 

d) Axe, felling, trade pattern AFTP 

10.1.1 The handle may also be marked with the I SI Certification 
Mark. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the piovisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations 
made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys 
the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that 
standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which 
is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI marked products 
are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a further 
safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI 
Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained 
from the Indian Standards Institution. 



APPENDIX A 

( Clause 4.2 ) 
TREATMENT OF GREEN BLANKS 

A-1. For the treatment, the green blanks shall be converted to the sizes as 
close as possible to the shape and dimensions of the handles ( allowing 
some oversize for shrinkage and final finishing ) and immediately immersed 
in a 40 percent (w/w) solution of polyethylene glycol ( PEG }-1500 or 60 
percent ( w/w ) solution of urea for approximately 24 hours. 

A-2. The blanks after the treatment as mentioned above shall be air- or 
kiln-seasoned in the usual manner until the desired moisture content is 
attained; The finishing of handles shall be done at the end. 

* General requirements for wooden tool handles ( third revision ).
